transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Chris Park (CTO - Maple Financial), Aisha Khan (Eng Lead), Ben Torres (Platform Ops)
Agenda: QBR / health check — usage, cost, reliability, roadmap alignment, security

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE for Maple. We're gonna run through the quarter — usage, costs, reliability, and then the roadmap bits. Liam is here for the tech deep dive.
[00:12] Chris Park: Hey Maya, thanks. Appreciate it. Happy to go over the numbers.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Hi all, Liam here. I'll jump in when we talk infra and benchmarks.
[00:25] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha. I'll mostly focus on the engineering constraints and any blockers.
[00:30] Ben Torres: Ben from platform. I'll answer network/ops questions.

[01:10] Maya Chen: Quick high-level summary before we dig in — your token usage is up about 38% month-over-month, cost is up ~45% largely because of more long-form generation and more retries during peak times. We flagged two latency incidents in late Feb where p95 jumped above 1.2s for a handful of requests. Liam, did you want to add context?
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, from the telemetry what I saw — there were a couple of sustained bursts that exceeded the usual sequencing, and the auto-batcher ended up queuing longer than expected, so tails popped up. Also noticed a couple of large requests that were near the 4k token cap and those push the KV cache working set. Might be "KV cash" in the transcript sometimes, sorry for my accent there.

[02:05] Chris Park: Right, those were during a promotional send where the chat summaries triggered after long sessions. Our ops team logged more retries. We saw cost spike because of retries plus we switched models mid-month from the base open model to a higher-quality variant.
[02:30] Maya Chen: Makes sense. Aisha, are those prompts you can trim or are they business-critical?
[02:35] Aisha Khan: The long prompts are partly business-critical — compliance summaries and regulatory notes. We tried truncating a bit but accuracy suffered. We do want the higher-quality variant for certain flows though.

[03:05] Maya Chen: Okay, so tradeoff between quality and unit cost. A few levers we discussed: dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles for lower-cost models. Liam — can you explain how caching would help these long-sessions?
[03:25] Liam O'Connor: Sure. For chat sessions where there are repeated instructions or boilerplate, our prefix cache can avoid recomputing tokens and reduce the per-request compute. For long recordings the KV cache keeps the attention states warm; if your session patterns are similar the hit rate improves. There's also model quantization — you can sometimes move to a int8-ish flavor and get 20-40% cost savings with minimal quality loss on some workloads. But we should run A/Bs.

[04:10] Ben Torres: For Dedicated, what's the lock-in or network picture? We need to know VPC peering, IP allowlists.
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated can be run in Redwood's managed pool, or in Private mode inside your VPC/prem. For VPC we provide connectors, SAML/SSO integration, and KMS options. We'll share network diagrams. There's no code-level lock-in — it's a serving endpoint — but Dedicated does require commit-level pricing.

[04:50] Chris Park: On security, our security team asked for SOC2, SSO, and key management docs — plus evidence of audit logs.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Yes — Liam will send the SOC2 report and our audit log/extract docs after the call. He'll also include KMS/HSM guidance.

[05:30] Chris Park: Cool. Also, curious about reliability SLOs — we have internal SLAs to meet. Can you confirm typical p99 and p95 targets on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: For hosted API our typical observed p95 is around 300-450ms for short requests, but p99 can vary with tails — usually under 900ms for typical models. Dedicated offers tighter tails because you get reserved capacity and can tune autoscaling; we've seen p99s under 500ms in many customers' Dedicated setups but depends on model and sequence length. We can run a dedicated benchmark with your exact prompt set.

[06:20] Aisha Khan: Would Dedicated also help with the retries we've seen? Our ops saw retries triggered by 429s and occasional timeouts during the promotional bursts.
[06:28] Maya Chen: Yes — Dedicated reduces noisy-neighbor variance and gives predictable throughput limits. We can also set graceful degradation and automatic fallbacks to a lower-cost variant when load is high.

[07:00] Chris Park: What's the expected delta in cost if we move, assuming we do a 3-node Dedicated pool versus staying on Hosted with batching/caching optimizations?
[07:10] Maya Chen: Ballpark — it's workload dependent. If you commit to reserved capacity you pay a fixed monthly for nodes; unit cost per token usually drops 20–35% versus fully on-demand hosted, and with batching/caching you could see additional 10–25% savings. We'll run a cost model with your traffic patterns.

[07:50] Liam O'Connor: Also worth noting that Dedicated gives you predictable tail behavior because the runtime can pre-warm KV cache and avoid some kernel cold starts. But Dedicated does require a commit and there is a ramp for autoscaling policies.

[08:30] Maya Chen: On the roadmap side, Maple had requested two features: 1) per-route token cost breakdown in the console, and 2) an easy rollback for model rollouts. Wanted to confirm those are still priority.
[08:42] Chris Park: Yes. Per-route cost is high priority — product wants to understand cost per feature. Rollbacks are also important for compliance.

[09:05] Liam O'Connor: We actually have a roadmap item for improved per-route analytics this quarter. Rollback APIs and canary deploys are supported today but we can add a policy to make rollback automatic on quality regressions — we need to tie it to your evals.

[09:40] Aisha Khan: For evals, we'd like to include our compliance prompts so we can detect regressions. Can we run automated evals on rollout?
[09:48] Liam O'Connor: Yes — the rollout tooling supports hooking an eval suite; if threshold drops we can fail the rollout. We'll help set up the eval harness for your prompts.

[10:20] Chris Park: One more on security — data residency. Some of our customers require EU residency. Are there region guarantees?
[10:28] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood supports region pinning in hosted and Dedicated; for Private we can run inside your VPC in specific cloud regions or on-prem. We'll get you the region SLA matrix.

[11:00] Ben Torres: Network-wise, if we go Private in our VPC, how do updates/deployments work? We want to avoid surprises during maintenance windows.
[11:08] Liam O'Connor: Private deployments are customer-managed control plane; updates are scheduled and we support canary windowed deploys. We'll share the maintenance calendar and deployment procedures.

[11:40] Maya Chen: Okay let's pivot to concrete next steps — we proposed a benchmark. Lily — sorry, Ben, you mentioned you'd provide traffic distribution and sample prompts?
[11:50] Ben Torres: Yes, I'll put together a 24-hour synthetic load distribution and a canonical prompt set (about ~500 queries) and share S3 link.

[12:08] Chris Park: We'll also need the pricing scenarios so Finance can sign off. Can you include committed usage tiers and a comparison of expected monthly cost on Hosted vs 3-node Dedicated?
[12:18] Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll include committed pricing, break-even analysis, and options for burst capacity.

[12:40] Aisha Khan: On the engineering side, can you outline the integration steps for SSO and KMS? We prefer SAML SSO and AWS KMS for key management.
[12:50] Liam O'Connor: We have a SAML guide and an AWS KMS integration doc. For Private we provide a KMS proxy pattern for encryption-at-rest. I'll include step-by-step.

[13:20] Chris Park: About the latency incidents — can we get a post-mortem of the Feb 27th spike? We need root cause for our audit trail.
[13:28] Liam O'Connor: Yes, I'll compile a short post-mortem: timeline, traces, affected bucket, and mitigation steps. Initial read is burst-induced batching tail and a model variant change mid-day causing cache churn.

[14:02] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else from Maple?
[14:08] Chris Park: No, that's it. Thanks.

[14:20] Maya Chen: Cool. To recap: action items and owners — Maya to send revised pricing and cost model; Liam to send SOC2 + KMS + network diagrams + post-mortem; Ben to share traffic and prompt set; we'll schedule the Dedicated benchmark for the week of 2026-03-09.

[14:40] Aisha Khan: Sounds good.

[14:48] Ben Torres: I'll get the artifacts over by 3/8.

[15:10] Maya Chen: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with the scheduling poll and links.

[15:18] Chris Park: Thanks, Maya and team.

[15:22] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mis-words ("KV cash", "Dedicate" for Dedicated), speaker overlap occasionally.

References mentioned: Pricing deck (link to be sent), SOC2 report (to be sent), Benchmark harness (we'll schedule), sample prompt set (Maple to provide).

End of meeting.
